look_here_first: Check the thick, often somewhat fleshy narrow alternate leaves and the long terminal cluster of small yellow heads, often borne predominantly on one side of branches. Coastal wet-saline habitat is a supporting cue, not proof by itself.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved source pool / Master Plant Pool
project_inclusion.range_basis: B070 deep review recognizes an Atlantic/Gulf coastal marsh and dune species; no confirmed native county among the inland project target counties. Cultivated Central Texas records do not establish native range.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Not counted as a confirmed target-zone native unless a separate three-county PASS review is completed.

best_field_traits: Rhizomatous perennial goldenrod of coastal marshes, dunes, and brackish margins.
Leaves alternate, comparatively thick and narrow; inspect leaf texture and venation rather than flower color.
Numerous small yellow composite heads in a terminal, often one-sided inflorescence.
Inflorescence architecture and fleshy leaf texture together are more useful than plant height.
Check mature involucres and foliage against closely related seaside goldenrods before final ID.

comparisons.key_distinctions: The seaside-goldenrod complex needs current accepted-name and geographic context; older references may fold S. mexicana into S. sempervirens. Inland S. altissima and S. canadensis typically have thinner serrate, three-nerved leaves and broader arching panicles; S. gigantea also differs in stem surface and inland ecology. Confirm with leaf thickness, venation, heads, and range together.
